issue.title: just check fails at lint (symvision): stale --epic-symbol entries for closed sase-rd.5
issue.description:
## CI failure

- **Node:** `just _lint-symvision`

`just check` fails at lint (symvision) before any test lane runs:

```
Error: --epic-symbol 'sase-rd.5(update_snippet)': bead 'sase-rd.5' is closed. Remove this stale --epic-symbol entry and clean up the symbol.
Error: --epic-symbol 'sase-rd.5(SnippetsPanel)': bead 'sase-rd.5' is closed. Remove this stale --epic-symbol entry and clean up the symbol.
```

Justfile still passes those two `--epic-symbol` flags (around lines 336-337) even though epic `sase-rd` (Snippet catalog, CLI, and ACE panel) is closed. The same error is produced by `just _lint-symvision` on this tree with no Justfile edits in the current diff. Removing the two stale entries is the fix; do not leave closed-bead epic-symbol waivers in the recipe.

This is unrelated to audited artifact-read metadata work; it blocks every agent's `just check` on this host because the gate runs before tests.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic: just _lint-symvision / just check fail with 'bead sase-rd.5 is closed. Remove this stale --epic-symbol entry' for both Justfile lines. A rerun on the same tree fails the same way; this is not intermittent.

payload.entry: Verified on clean master b7bdd3185 by running just _lint-symvision: it exits successfully with All public/private classes/functions are used properly. Commit 4f87eb4b2 removed both stale sase-rd.5 epic-symbol entries from Justfile when the Snippets panel work landed. Neither closed-bead waiver remains, so the lint blocker described here is gone.

payload.close_reason: 4f87eb4b2 removed both stale sase-rd.5 symvision waivers and the symvision gate now passes.

evidence.note: Independently reproduced on 2026-10-20: just _lint-symvision and sase tool run check both fail because five --epic-symbol flags still name closed phase sase-1nf.10.1.3; the named check stops before the test lane. This is the same stale closed-epic whitelist failure as this bead, recurring with a new closed phase.
